hero.name: Oversized headline with one live word
hero.from: x.ai ('for everything you build / imagine / search'), Vercel, Stripe Sessions
hero.job: Type does the work, for a brief without a strong photograph: an oversized headline across the container where one word changes (what you move, where you ship, who it is for), then a foot row with the line and the buttons on the left half and four facts as a column on the right half.

grid.h1: span-12 from the left line, its two lines locked (layout.js), the live word last
grid.foot: the lead and the buttons under it on span-6; the four facts as a column (label left, value right, hairlines) on span-5 start-8, ending on the right line

at1440.h1: 144 (129.6 after the 0.9 scale) on 2 lines from y 227, 1280 wide from x 80; the lines locked, the live word's slot as wide as its widest word
at1440.underline: the accent, 0.05em thick, under the live word only; each word brings its own
at1440.foot: 64 under the h1: the lead 20/30 on 3 lines on span-6, the buttons 44 32 under it; the four facts as a column on span-5 start-8 (rows of 50, hairlines), ending on the right line
at1440.measured: hero 900/900, h1 130px (weight 400) on 2 lines, its box from y 227

at390.measured: hero 844/844, h1 49px on 3 lines from y 149

hero.moment: the live word (data-ly-word): a new word every 2 s for two rounds, then it rests on the first and plays again when the pointer enters; no line moves (the slot is as wide as the widest word). Letters near the pointer thicken (+200) and widen (+10%) on a face with a wdth axis (data-ly-letters=wdth), on lines locked at rest. A phone and reduced motion hold the first word, no letters
mistakes: a slogan; the sentence must say what is sold
more than four words in the rotation
a word that changes the line's meaning into nonsense
the underline on the whole headline
a face without a wght axis for the letters
a line that breaks differently when the word changes or a letter widens
the moments kit's word-rotate on top of the live word
dealt to a brief that has photographs (a photograph leads then)
